messages:
violet: Heads-up — saw a hang in py-sdk 0.9.2 when cancelling SSE streams. Repro steps below, pretty weird: finalizers/weakrefs not running and event loop gets stuck.

violet: Minimal repro:
```py
async def main():
    client = RedwoodClient()
    gen = client.stream("/v1/generate", {...})  # async generator
    task = asyncio.create_task(consume(gen))
    await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
    task.cancel()  # sometimes cancels cleanly, sometimes hangs

async def consume(gen):
    async for chunk in gen:
        pass
```

violet: If I rely on __del__/weakref finalizer to close the underlying aiohttp response, it doesn't always run. On Python 3.11 on mac, sometimes the whole process stays alive.

aj: ugh. can you paste the stack trace when it hangs?

violet: stack trace snippet (attached to thread):
```
Task exception was never retrieved
Future exception was never retrieved
File \".../site-packages/aiohttp/streams.py\", line 200, in __del__
  self._transport.close()
RuntimeError: Event loop is closed
```

aj: that suggests finalizer ran after loop shutdown; we shouldn't rely on __del__ for cleanup. we need an explicit close() or async context manager.

sam: we already have `StreamingResponse.__aiter__` that returns an async generator but the public API doesn't enforce `async with` usage. that's a usability bug — users assume `for` will auto-cleanup.

violet: Agreed. Could be a typing/typing-helpers doc issue too — the hints show `Iterator[bytes]` for sync/async combos which confuses users.

aj: quick patch idea: add a `__aenter__/__aexit__` pair on the stream object and document `async with client.stream() as s:` pattern. Also add a finalizer that logs (not closes) if loop is gone.

sam: also add `aclose()` on generator object so `await gen.aclose()` works in cancellations. That maps to `AsyncIterator.aclose` semantics.

violet: I tested locally by adding `await gen.aclose()` on cancel path and it consistently cleaned up. can send PR with tests.

aj: plz file GH issue and link here. include matrix of python versions and whether test harness uses `asyncio.get_event_loop()` vs `get_running_loop()`.

violet: done: https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-sdk/issues/842 — added failing test that hangs on CI reproducibly on mac-latest/3.11.

ci-bot: CI failed for branch fix/stream-aclose — 1 failing test (tests/streams/test_cancel.py::test_generator_hang)

sam: I'll take a look. probable cause: we rely on weakref.finalize calling into synchronous close which uses loop.call_soon_threadsafe under the hood — not safe during interpreter shutdown.

aj: propose we: 1) export `aclose()` on the async generator wrapper, 2) add `async with` support and docs, 3) update examples to show cancellation pattern:
```py
async with client.stream(...) as gen:
    async for chunk in gen:
        if should_cancel:
            await gen.aclose()
            break
```

aj: also add a runtime warning if generator garbage-collected without explicit close while loop still running.

violet: tests pass locally after aclose implementation. i'll open the PR. leaving this thread as reference for release notes. cc @release-bot

release-bot: Noted — include streaming-cancel-fix in 0.9.3 changelog and mention breaking doc change (recommend async with).

sam: nice. also add a small note in devex docs about typing: show `AsyncIterator[StreamChunk]` and sample type-stub for `client.stream(...) -> AsyncIterator[StreamChunk]`.

violet: Thanks all. follow-ups: (1) PR link when ready, (2) add a small migration note for customers relying on GC finalizers, (3) maybe add a telemetry counter for unclosed streams.

aj: SG. thanks for catching this. :thumbsup:
